summary: I.1 accepts direct awaited nouns, temporal objects, l-marked persons/vehicles, suffixes and clauses; I.2 also has direct objects. At 6/54 the same nəṭrət first means waiting, then guarding cattle; argument marking alone cannot determine sense.
I.2 includes self-protection with ruḥa, graves and shepherds' duty even while sleeping. JTM 3.1/22 and MAC Mother Mary/34 show protection from harm; II combines waiting and divine safeguarding.
I.3 'to expect' overlaps I.1 'erwarten'. Preserve the existing numbers and Joseph filing. No renumbering or silent merger.
Contracted -ll-/-nn- sequences occur in waiting and guarding; exact segmentation needs confirmation. Infectum-wa presents habitual or rotating watch; repeated Preterit marks prolonged waiting.
Glossary searches for darbo, nuṭri-lxu and naṭər ruḥ plus the complete supplied entry found no matching nṭr idiom record. Similar path-watching under ʕyš is a different verb.

Singular naṭər and plural naṭiri in past narrative are provisionally grouped under Preterit Intransitive rather than inventing a Part act. contrast from identical qaṭəl shapes. The regular inherited Preterit remains nṭəlle.
nṭiro we is a result/state expression with expected propositional content; it supports a Detransitive Part. Pass. cell, not a complete finite Detransitive system.
The Classical Syriac speech at Jan 2.10/2755, 2779 and 2795 is kept separate from Turoyo evidence. Lexical Nəṭuro guard is not evidence for verbal Part act.
Routine guarding/waiting cells already filled by round 1 are not filled again. One I.2 Infectum-wa addition reaches five; I.3 reaches five after the inherited split example is counted once.

Proverbial m-marked caution is semantically different from expected source m-. Round-1 ruḥo self-protection idiom does not duplicate this construction. No new idiom is proposed, so no cross-entry idiom lookup was needed.

Is nṭr darbo conventional or an occasional metonymy? Confirm segmentation in gnoṭanne, noṭannox and Knoṭannəx.

Confirm naṭər/naṭiri as finite Preterit Intransitive rather than participial predicates, and reduced nəṭriwo in Jan 1.53/2567.
